title: RRB Group D 28 Nov 2025 Shift 1 - Mathematics - Problems on Ages
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: The present age of a father is twice the sum of the present ages of his two sons. After 20 years, the father's age will be equal to the sum of his sons' ages. Find the present age of the father.
questions.explain:
Let the present sum of the ages of his two sons be $S$. Thus, father's present age $F = 2S$.
After 20 years:
Father's age = $F + 20$
Sum of the two sons' ages = $S + 20 + 20 = S + 40$ (since both sons age by 20 years).
According to the problem: $F + 20 = S + 40$
Substitute $F = 2S$: $2S + 20 = S + 40 \Rightarrow S = 20$.
The father's present age $F = 2(20) = 40$ years.

questions.q: A father is 5 times as old as his son. If the sum of their ages is 54 years, how old is the son?
questions.explain:
Let the son's present age be $x$ years.
Then the father's age is $5x$ years.
According to the question, $x + 5x = 54$.
$6x = 54 \Rightarrow x = 9$.
The son is 9 years old.
